statement: Production deploys are frozen Fridays after 2 PM PT and on company holidays
Code review: 2 approvals for Tier 0 and Tier 1 services, 1 for Tier 2 and 3
On-call v3: 1-week rotations, at most 1 in 4 weeks, Sev1 ack within 5 min on Tier 0 and Tier 1
Postmortems due within 5 business days for Sev1 and Sev2
Access reviews are quarterly (cycles open first business day of Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct; 15 business days per reviewer)
Vulnerability SLAs: Critical 7 days, High 30 days
Secrets rotation every 90 days
Logs, traces, and dataset archives: 30 days hot, 13 months archive
Disaster recovery for Tier 0 and Tier 1: RPO 15 min, RTO 4 hours
Prod access requires a hardware security key (FIDO2/WebAuthn); backup key registered
An ADR is required if more than one team is affected
Open-source licenses: approved list only; copyleft needs legal review
Service tiering: Tier 0 core platform, Tier 1 customer-facing, Tier 2 internal, Tier 3 experimental
Customer SLA: Enterprise 99.95%, Team and Free 99.9%
Data classification: customer-derived data is Confidential by default; Restricted reserved for credentials, payment card data, and regulated identifiers
Each new team namespace on Kestrel gets 40 CPU cores by default; increases go through a ticket to COMP
All builds and deploys run through TechSync Ship and Gatekeeper CI; Jenkins was retired in May 2026
Meridian Mesh default per-route request timeout is 15 seconds
Platform-owned services must soak in staging for at least 60 minutes before prod
Gatekeeper CI prod canary sends 5% of traffic for 15 minutes
New services are onboarded as Kestrel namespaces through a COMP ticket (no per-service VM pools since the 2019 Kubernetes migration)
OBS on-call must acknowledge Sev1 pages on Lookout within 3 minutes
Approved exception: automated kestrel-image-bot node-image patch PRs (images/node/ only) need 1 approval; all other Kestrel changes follow company policy
MOB app-store submissions may go out during the production freeze; other Mobile deploys including Pushline stay frozen
Ledger invoice data is classified Restricted
Ledger Core service API keys rotate every 90 days (180 days before Jan 2025)
Pushline retries a failed delivery at most 3 times, then dead-letters it
A deprecated Ledger public API version is supported for 12 months after the deprecation notice
Quarry default query timeout is 120 seconds
Insight reached GA in June 2024 for all tiers (beta in 2023 was Enterprise only)
Console is owned by Web in Product Engineering; platform and cluster issues escalate to PLAT Compute
TechSync Mobile minimum iOS is 16 (was 15 before March 2026)
Ledger Core invoice schema and public API changes need an ADR even if only PAY is affected, approved by PAY EM and Tech Lead
Enterprise availability target for Pushline push delivery to APNs and FCM is 99.9% (approved exception)
Console is Tier 1
Keystone (Tier 0) Sev1 pages must be acknowledged within 5 minutes. The ITC runbook's 15-minute figure is not authoritative (no approved exception)
Vaultline dynamic secrets have a maximum lease of 1 hour
Customer-derived data is Confidential by default; Restricted reserved for credentials, payment card data and regulated identifiers
Keystone SSO sessions last at most 8 hours; apps including Console cannot extend
Reservoir tables are partitioned daily by event date
Full threat-model review before staging for DSEC services; exception: lightweight checklist for the 3 named Foundry research sandboxes only
Sentinel scans every pull request; an open Critical finding blocks merge
Critical findings on SEC-owned services (Sentinel, Vaultline) must be fixed within 3 days
GPL/LGPL allowed in ITC internal-only tools without per-use legal review, logged in ITC license register; AGPL excluded
Access review evidence must be uploaded to Compass for every in-scope system, Tier 3 included
